header.name: Distribution of Sequences in Number Theory
header.description: This course introduces the study of how number theoretic sequences are distributed modulo one. The sequences of interest arise from various areas, including physics, cryptographic considerations, and naturally occurring sequences in number theory problems. Recent years have seen several developments in this field. In this course, we will examine some of these results, beginning with a the classical theory of uniform distribution of sequences. We will then explore the finer structure of sequence distribution, focusing on level spacing measures and correlation measures. Throughout the course, we shall study these global and local aspects of distribution for different sequences.
prerequisites_mandatory: MTH 240: Real Analysis I or equivalent
MTH 340: Real Analysis II or equivalent

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the concept of equidistribution modulo one, both qualitatively using Weyl's criterion and quantitatively using discrepancy.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Apply Weyl’s criterion and exponential sums to study sequences of interest.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the finer structure of sequences via gap distribution and correlation measures.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the distribution of prime number sequences, Farey sequences, fractional parts of polynomial sequences, Farey fractions.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Connect the theory of distribution of sequences to applications in harmonic analysis, numerical integration, random number generation and mathematical finance.

lecture_topics: Background and Motivation from Diophantine approximation and Benford's law
Basic notions: equidistribution modulo one, Weyl's criterion, Fejer's theorem
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment on equidistribution and Weyl's criterion

lecture_topics: Applications of Weyl's criterion to polynomial, logarithmic sequences.
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment on applications of Weyl's criterion and computing discrepancy

lecture_topics: Introduction to finer notions of distribution of sequences and motivation from physics.
Basic notions: Gap distribution, correlation measure, pair correlation and the relationship between them
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment involving notions of finer structure and their relationship

lecture_topics: Understanding pair correlation and gap distribution of various number theoretic sequences such as prime number sequences, Farey fractions, and polynomial sequences.
Applications to numerical integration, random-number generation, etc.

resources.title: L. Kuipers and H. Niederreiter: Uniform Distribution of Sequences, Wiley-Interscience, 2012
Hugh L. Montgomery: Ten Lectures on the Interface between Analytic Number Theory and Harmonic Analysis, CBMS, 1994
M. Drmota and R. F. Tichy: Sequences, Discrepancies and Applications
